### Wall Street Closes in a Correction With the Nasdaq Down 2.49 Percent and Nvidia Down 4.12 Percent at $156.14, the Board Is Reported Not Discussing Mr. Huang&rsquo;s Return as the Petition Passes 180,000, the President Departs for Manila Saying Ukraine Will Be Talked About in Shenzhen and Mr. Kim May Come, and Chairman Warsh Sets Out Three Scenarios for Super Intelligence While Alaska&rsquo;s Count Still Waits

Filed as: Edition No. 56 — The Evening Watch · 2026-11-16T18:00:00-05:00 · https://objectivedailynews.com/editions/2026-11-16-evening-watch.html

The Evening File — The Desk’s Report

 Objective

 Wall Street Closes in a Correction With the Nasdaq Down 2.49 Percent and Nvidia Down 4.12 Percent at $156.14, the Board Is Reported Not Discussing Mr. Huang’s Return as the Petition Passes 180,000, the President Departs for Manila Saying Ukraine Will Be Talked About in Shenzhen and Mr. Kim May Come, and Chairman Warsh Sets Out Three Scenarios for Super Intelligence While Alaska’s Count Still Waits

 The evening file: a market that closed in a correction on the day before the chipmaker reports; a board reported not discussing the return its petitioners demand, and a rule that closes the rental route the scandal ran through; a chairman who priced the new technology three ways and moved no rate; a president airborne for Manila with Ukraine on his own agenda and a fourth leader possibly to come; a recovery counted at 330 by half past one and a funding fight that gained its sharpest sentences; a European seat that Moscow says was never agreed; and a count in Alaska that spent a third day where Saturday left it.

 By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 1800 ET, Monday, November 16, 2026. This edition completes the day continued in Edition No. 55, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 today, in Edition No. 54, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 today, in Edition No. 53, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 today, and in Edition No. 52, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Sunday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the evening figures differ from the noon figures, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Evening in Brief: A Correction at the Close, a Departure in the Morning, and a Count That Did Not Move

Monday settled the shape of its recovery, the words of its confirmation, and the price of its largest company, and it left the same four facts open that the midday file left open. Wall Street closed lower for a third straight session, with the Nasdaq Composite down 2.49 percent in the closing account filed below and in a correction by the wire’s measure, and Nvidia down 4.12 percent at $156.14 on the day the board was reported not discussing its founder’s return, in the board account filed below. The President departed for Asia in the morning with Ukraine on his own stated agenda and a possible fourth leader named, in the Press account filed below. Chairman Warsh spoke at noon in San Francisco and gave the day its only set speech, in the wire account filed below. The airlines ran at 330 cancellations by 1330, in the wire’s updated count filed below, and the argument over the money to prevent a second Friday gained its sentences from both sides, in the funding account filed below. Alaska’s count did not move. The desk takes the files in that order. What the day settled is printed first in each file; what it left open is printed last, and the open list is unchanged in kind: the root cause of Friday’s stop, the condition of the radar at Al-Riffa, the call in Alaska, and the board’s own word, which Monday supplied only at second hand.

The Markets at the Close: A Third Lower Session, the Chip Index Down 5.28 Percent, and Oil Down With the Stocks

The closes are agreed across the accounts, and the desk prints them once. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.49 percent to 24,509.76, the S&P 500 fell 1.92 percent to 7,416.59, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 739.38 points, or 1.41 percent, to 51,608.17, in the closing account above and in the closing summary filed below; the Press rounded the same closes to 2.5 and 1.9 percent, in the brief account filed below. The wire reported that the Nasdaq now stands more than 10 percent below its October 6 high, which puts it in a correction, in the closing account. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 5.28 percent, its second straight heavy session after Friday’s 3.43 percent, with Micron down 7.62 percent, Intel and Dell each down about 7 percent, and AMD down 5.58 percent, in the same account; only consumer staples and utilities finished higher among the eleven sectors, and the volatility index rose 19.84 percent to 23.13, in the same account. Asia’s closes stand where the midday file printed them final: Taiwan down 6.03 percent, the Kospi down 3.59 percent, the Nikkei down 2.4 percent. Oil fell with the stocks: West Texas crude at $85.35, down 3.62 percent, and Brent at $92.16, down 3.84 percent, in the closing account’s late quotes, against Brent near $95.40 in the Asia readings the overnight file carried; gold futures stood at $3,853.10, down 0.85 percent, and Bitcoin at $64,930.74 at 1616, down 0.59 percent, in the same account. The ten-year Treasury yield closed at 5.12 percent, down from 5.15 percent on Friday, and the New York Fed’s November manufacturing index fell to 7.8 from 25.5, against a forecast of 17.6, in the same account. The accounts name three causes together and none alone: the fallout from Mr. Huang’s exit, the Commerce Department’s new rule on rented chips, and caution ahead of Nvidia’s report on Tuesday and Anthropic’s pricing on Wednesday, in the closing account. Settled: the closes, and the correction. Open: Tuesday’s report, which every account in the file names as the next fact.

Nvidia at the Close: A Board Reported Not Discussing a Return, a Petition Past 180,000, and a President Open to One

The board’s position reached the file on Monday at second hand, and it is a refusal to discuss, not a statement. A person familiar with the matter told CNBC that the board is not discussing bringing Mr. Huang back and is focused on the investigation into his conduct, in the board account above; the Financial Times reported the same day that the board has not put a return on the table for review, in the same account. No statement from the board itself, from the company, or from the interim chief, Ms. Kress, stands in the evening file. The investigation’s shape stands in the same accounts: the law firm Wachtell Lipton has been retained to examine whether Mr. Huang’s conduct endangered national security or company secrets, in the board account and in the plans account filed below. Those are the questions the inquiry is reported to ask; no finding by the board, by any committee, or by any court on any allegation in this file has been made, and the desk prints the allegations as allegations. The campaign’s counters moved again on Monday and are printed apart, at their hours: more than 168,000 signatures at midday in the midday file; 182,552 displayed at 1255 Eastern, with 8,974 self-identified employees, in the agenda account filed below; more than 180,000 in the board account and in the plans account; and over 185,600 in the Caller account filed below. The affiliations on the petition are self-reported and unverified, in the agenda account. The President said on Monday that he was open to Mr. Huang returning, in the plans account and the board account; Mr. Gerstner of Altimeter Capital, named among the campaign’s investors, told CNBC that Mr. Huang had not discussed a comeback with him, in the same accounts; and one analyst’s sentence stands against the whole file, in the Caller account: “We see no chance Jensen comes back to Nvidia as CEO.” The Financial Times’ Sunday report, that Mr. Huang has discussed a return with confidants, stands unamended beside the board’s reported position, and the two do not meet. Morgan Stanley cut its 2027 and 2028 data center sales estimates by about 10 percent, in the closing account. Earnings stand on Tuesday at about 1620 Eastern, with a call at 1700: consensus revenue at $109.1 billion and earnings per share at $2.47 in the closing account, against the company’s own outlook of $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2 percent, in the same account, and the three midday readings of $108.7 billion, $108.93 billion and about $109.2 billion standing in the midday file. Settled: the board is not discussing a return, on the reporting. Open: everything the board has not said itself.

The Commerce Rule: The Rental Route Closed, Five Countries Named, and Ninety Days to a Licence

The Administration’s first policy answer to the scandal arrived on Monday, and it is a licensing rule. The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule so that the existing restrictions, in its words, “cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries,” in the loophole account filed below. A licence is required for covered chips going to a data centre anywhere in the world that provides more than 12 million in aggregate total processing performance to a company headquartered in China, Macau, or another listed country, or whose ultimate parent is headquartered there, in the rule account filed below, which reckons the threshold at roughly 750 H100 processors or about 330 Blackwell B200s by the rule’s formula. Centres already selling that much computing power to such companies have 90 days from the rule’s taking effect to obtain a licence, and exporters will need a licence to send advanced chips and servers to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, which the rule names as carrying a higher-than-normal risk of diversion, in the same accounts; the one carve-out named is computing used only for commercial recommender systems, in the rule account. The rule formally rescinds the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule, in both accounts, and it takes effect when it appears in the Federal Register, which had not happened in the accounts the desk read, with comments due 60 days after publication, in the rule account. The company at the centre of the file stands inside it: the Singapore company where the woman named in the allegations worked is suspected of selling remote access to American chips to Chinese firms, says it operates lawfully, and has opened an internal review, in the closing account. The President said the same day that selling other chips is “a good thing,” in the same account. No finding against any company named in this file stands in the evening file. Settled: the rule, its threshold, and its five countries. Open: its effective date, and what it does to Tuesday’s guidance.

Chairman Warsh at Noon: Three Scenarios for Super Intelligence, No Forecast, and No Rate Proposed

The chairman’s remarks, which began at the hour the midday edition was stamped, are the day’s set speech, and the desk prints their structure whole. Speaking in San Francisco at the opening of the Productivity and Jobs Task Force Conference, Chairman Warsh said the staff have begun modelling what the technology he calls super intelligence could do to the economy, and set out three scenarios, in the wire account above and in the scenarios account filed below. In the first, the technology raises productivity and the gains are shared broadly across labour and the owners of capital: “In that event, real GDP growth rises persistently above its long-run average, and the US stays close to full employment,” in the wire account. In the second, the gains arrive and the workers are left behind, with unemployment rising even as the economy grows, in the scenarios account. In the third, the heavy investment disappoints, equity valuations fall, and unemployment rises, in the same account. “These are illustrative scenarios, not forecasts,” the chairman said, in the same account; “Our job is to prepare for whatever comes next,” in the wire account. The technology could prove distinct from earlier technologies as a force to “supercharge idea generation,” he said, and machines that can amass or exceed human knowledge are still machines and do not take the place of human judgment, morality, or responsibility, in the growth account filed below. “Our role in all this is neither advocacy nor opposition,” he said, in the wire account. “Our responsibility is to recognize that the widespread adoption of this technology will have significant impact on the economy, with important implications for monetary policy down the road. The big questions are about magnitude, scope, and timing.” A second central bank voice entered the file the same day: Governor Barr warned that the construction boom is increasingly financed through arrangements whose potential maximum value the bank estimates at more than $3 trillion off balance sheet, in the scenarios account. The chairman proposed no change in interest rates, in every account; the markets’ pricing stands where the week left it, fully priced for a quarter-point rise at the December 8 and 9 meeting in the midday file, and at 95.7 percent for a quarter-point rise in December in the closing account’s reading of the futures. The minutes of the October 27 and 28 meeting, at which rates were held at 3.75 to 4 percent, are published on Wednesday, in the scenarios account. Settled: the scenarios, and that they are not forecasts. Open: which of the three the economy is in, which no speaker on Monday claimed to know.

The President’s Road: A Morning Departure, Ukraine on His Own Agenda, and a Fourth Leader Who May Come

The President left Washington on Monday morning, and his own words before departure moved two files at once. He departed for Manila, where he attends the ASEAN summit on Tuesday, meets the leaders of India, Japan and Australia in the Quad, signs the trade deal with Thailand, and receives a state visit welcome on Wednesday, and continues to Shenzhen for the APEC leaders’ meeting and Thursday’s three-way session, in the Press account above and in the departure account filed below. On Ukraine, his words and his officials’ words now stand apart in the open. His officials told reporters on Friday that the Shenzhen session would discuss nuclear disarmament and the Iran war and steer clear of Russia’s war with Ukraine, in the Press account; the President told reporters at the White House on Monday morning: “We’ll talk about, my favorite subject, Ukraine. Ukraine’s losing Ukraine. Russia is losing 25,000 soldiers in the month. So we’ll be talking about that,” in the same account. On a fourth leader, he said that Mr. Kim “may come” to Shenzhen but “that’s up to President Xi,” in the same account; the United Nations Secretary-General’s Monday words in Manila, that the United Nations is ready to support a denuclearisation programme and that it is not yet guaranteed the parties will get there, stand in the midday file. On the separate meeting that the file said was not planned, the Kremlin aide’s Monday sentence now stands against the White House’s: “I can say with 100% certainty that since both Putin and Donald Trump will be in Shenzhen, they will undoubtedly meet. We are currently discussing the character and location of the meeting,” Mr. Ushakov told reporters, in the Press account; the White House said the President and President Putin have no separate meeting planned, in the summit account in the morning’s reporting. President Zelenskyy’s concern, stated last month, stands in the Press account: “We really don’t want this to turn into ‘Yalta 2, 3, 4’ with a redistribution of influence.” The host’s words stand where the midday file printed them: the three leaders “will exchange views in depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations, which is of groundbreaking significance,” and neither nuclear arms nor Iran named in answer to the question that named both, in the confirmation account filed below. Mr. Musk travels with the President, in the Press account; Mr. Huang, who accompanied him on the May trip to China, does not, in the trip account filed below, and American officials have said the President does not intend to raise the spying matter with President Xi, in the Press account and the midday file. The meeting with Qatar’s prime minister that the overnight file scheduled for Monday in Washington stands in no account the desk read on Monday, and the desk says so plainly. Settled: the departure, and the meeting confirmed from all three sides. Open: the agenda, which now has four versions—Washington’s officials’, the President’s, Beijing’s, and the Kremlin aide’s—and whether a fourth chair is set in the room.

The Airlines at Evening: 330 Cancelled by 1330, a President’s Heart Attack, and a Ransom Named in Answer

Monday’s recovery held through the afternoon, and its last reading in the evening file is the wire’s updated count. By 1330 Eastern there were 330 flight cancellations and 3,000 delays, down from more than 2,300 cancelled and 11,000 delayed on Sunday, in the updated wire account filed below. The day’s series stands in the cocked hat: 55 of Monday’s flights cancelled as of Sunday evening, about 250 by 0400, 533 cancelled and 8,365 delayed by 0700 in the morning account in the midday file, 300 cancelled and 1,500 delayed as of 0900 in the wire’s first count, and 330 and 3,000 by 1330 in its update—readings at different hours on different bases, agreeing that the day ran in the hundreds against the thousands of each of the three days before it, which together stand at more than 18,000 cancellations in the wire’s count. Tuesday’s cancellations stand at 68 due to be cancelled, in the morning account in the midday file. No second stop was ordered on Monday in any account the desk read. On cause, the file gained no root cause on Monday: the Administration’s account stands at a router replaced at El Dorado, Arkansas, during copper-to-fibre work, a second router at Amarillo, Texas, installer error or faulty hardware undecided, and the Secretary’s Sunday admission that the root cause is not known, in the midday file and in the easing account in the morning’s reporting. The money argument gained its sharpest sentences from both sides on Monday, and the desk prints them as they were given. The President, weighing in on Monday, said he was “sure” Congress would soon give the Administration more money, and: “Essentially, what you saw on Friday was very, very old equipment that had a heart attack,” in the funding account above. The Secretary’s words stand in the same account: “I have systems that are from the ’90s. I have radar that are from the ’60s and ’70s.” Representative DeLauro, the senior Democrat on the House Appropriations Committee, answered that the money Congress has already designated “largely remains unspent” and called the ask a “$50 billion ransom without a real plan to deliver,” in the same account. Representative Larsen’s figure stands in the same account: $11 billion of the $12.5 billion remains unspent, and his question: “Explain to Congress, again, why they need more money?” The Secretary’s defence stands there too: all of that tranche will be spent and deployed by the end of 2028, and none of it could go to the telecommunications architecture he has to build, in the same account. Senator Van Hollen’s sentence stands between them, in the same account: Congress has “given the administration what they asked for,” and “If they need more, they should come up and justify it.” Two dated facts close the file: the Secretary sits in on the Senate Republicans’ weekly lunch on Tuesday to make the case, and as of Monday morning he had not released comprehensive details of how the $50 billion would be spent, in the same account; and the request has become a variable in the negotiations to avoid a shutdown after December 11, when government funding runs out, in the same account. Settled: the recovery, and the shape of the fight. Open: the root cause, the itemised plan, and whether Congress pays.

The Gulf and Europe at Evening: No New Word on the Radar, and No Agreement on the Europeans

The radar file gained no new word on Monday, and the desk records the silence as a fact of the file. The monitoring account that has followed the claim since Sunday closed its watch on Monday at midday with the file where the midday edition left it, in the monitoring account filed below: six drones targeted the radar at Al-Riffa in the Guards’ claim; several attacks intercepted and destroyed in Manama’s account; all drones intercepted and the claims false in the American Ambassador’s Sunday sentence; two drones shot down in Friday’s denial, which concerned Friday’s claim; no impacts to American forces in the Central Command spokesman’s sentence, which did not address the radar; and no assessment of the radar’s condition from any capital, in the explainer account filed below. The rest of the Gulf file stands where the night left it: three American carriers in the region in a force of more than 20 ships; the President’s Sunday words that new strikes are highly unlikely while negotiations progress; Tehran’s words that Iran remains in a state of war; the Khor Mor gas field strike in Iraq unclaimed, with the joint investigation ordered; and the supertanker claim in Hormuz unconfirmed. Europe’s file, by contrast, moved on Monday, and it moved against the weekend’s account. Mr. Ushakov said on Monday that the next round is being discussed in the existing three-way format, that no date has been set, and that on widening the format no agreement had been reached with Russia and many things would first have to be done for European participation to be acceptable, possibly after one or more further trilateral rounds, in the talks account filed below; the question of the Europeans joining will arise only when Moscow receives a clear signal from them about what they want and what constructive thing they can offer, in the condition account filed below. Those sentences stand against Mr. Kushner’s statement after meeting President Zelenskyy in Dublin that both sides had agreed to include Europeans, in the talks account, and against the Kremlin’s own Saturday signal that Moscow would accept whoever Europe sends, in the same account. The Kremlin spokesman’s Monday words stand in the midday file: the Union’s latest statements suggest a reluctance to contribute to the peace process, and Moscow hopes to hear directly from the Europeans. The prisoners’ channel stands where the midday file left it, in preparation: Russia’s human-rights commissioner in regular contact with her Ukrainian counterpart, a major exchange being prepared, no number and no date stated, against the Abu Dhabi agreement’s figures of 1,200 to 1,300 per side in the week’s file. No contact from Europe’s negotiators to Moscow stands in the evening file. Settled: the responses on the radar are complete and the machine is undescribed; the European seat is disputed by the capital that would grant it. Open: both.

Alaska and the Week: A Third Day at Saturday’s Count, and a Calendar That Runs to Thursday

Alaska’s count spent Monday where Saturday left it, and the evening file adds the calendar to the arithmetic. The Press’s count stands at Ms. Peltola 140,637 votes, 49.9 percent, and Senator Sullivan 129,424, 46.0 percent, an estimated 97 percent counted, in the markets account filed below, which is the Press’s Monday-morning count carried unchanged through the day in every account the desk read; no new count from the Division of Elections stands in the evening file, and the desk says so plainly for the third edition in succession. The figures around the count stand as the file has printed them: 49.94 percent on the full denominator, 157 votes short of a majority by the desk’s arithmetic, in the majority account filed below; 50.1 percent on the dashboard’s calculation, which excludes unresolved write-ins; a winner listed on one tracker; 99.8 cents on one market; a victory declared by Ms. Peltola on Saturday; and Senator Sullivan’s spokesman’s sentence unamended, that the campaign is still waiting for every ballot to be counted, in the markets account. One analysis in the file runs ahead of the count: the preliminary tally from the cast vote record, updated Monday morning Alaska time, has Ms. Peltola leading the ranked-choice count 51.8 percent to 48.2 percent if a tabulation is required, in the tally account filed below. It is a tally of a record that is not final, and the desk prints it as such. Overseas ballots may arrive through Wednesday, November 18, when the ranked-choice tabulation is scheduled if no candidate holds a majority; certification is targeted for November 25, in the same accounts. The week’s calendar is now the file’s largest settled fact, and the desk prints it once. Tuesday carries October retail sales, France’s nationwide strike on the eighth anniversary of the Yellow Vest movement, the Secretary’s lunch with Senate Republicans, and Nvidia’s earnings after the close. Wednesday carries the October meeting minutes, the first day of APEC in Shenzhen, Alaska’s tabulation, and Anthropic’s pricing, at a range of $70 to $78 for 825 million shares, in the closing account. Thursday carries the three presidents in Shenzhen, the police bill in the French Senate, Spain’s head-to-head debate, and Anthropic’s first trading day in New York. Spain votes on November 29; the Federal Reserve decides on December 8 and 9; government funding runs out after December 11. The Midnight Watch collects at 0000.

The Cocked Hat

Where the evening’s bearings do not meet, the desk prints the triangle. On the day’s flights: 55 cancelled as of Sunday evening, about 250 by 0400, 533 by 0700, 300 by 0900, and 330 by 1330—and on Sunday’s own total, more than 2,300 cancelled and 11,000 delayed in the wire’s against 2,858 and 26,392 in the morning account’s. On the money: billions in impact in the Secretary’s estimate, $345 million to the four largest airlines in the brokerage’s, $50 billion asked, $12.5 billion approved last year, $1 billion of it spent in the Democrats’ answer, $11 billion unspent in Representative Larsen’s, and a ransom without a plan in Representative DeLauro’s. On Shenzhen: nuclear arms and Iran in Washington’s officials’ telling and Ukraine off it, Ukraine on it in the President’s own Monday words, world peace and strategic stability in Beijing’s, no separate meeting in the White House’s account and a meeting beyond doubt in the Kremlin aide’s, and a fourth leader who may come, at the host’s invitation or not at all. On the board: a return discussed with confidants in the Sunday report, a return not discussed by the board in Monday’s, a president open to it, an investor who never heard of it from the man himself, an analyst who sees no chance of it, and a petition counted at 168,000, 180,000, 182,552 and 185,600 at four hours of the same day. On the technology: shared gains, displacement, and disappointment, in the chairman’s three scenarios, which are not forecasts. On the radar: six drones on target, several attacks destroyed, all drones intercepted, two drones down on Friday, no impacts to forces, and no word on the machine. On Europe: agreed in the envoy’s account, unagreed in the aide’s, and conditional in the same aide’s second sentence. On Alaska: 49.94 percent and 50.1 percent on two denominators, a winner listed and no call made, and no count at all on Monday. Inside the triangle is where the evening honestly stands.
